name: Lyndon B. Johnson
role: Oversaw the massive escalation: the Tonkin Gulf resolution, Rolling Thunder, the first Marines at Da Nang, and over 500,000 combat troops in country by 1968. Announced a partial bombing halt and his own withdrawal from the 1968 race on the same night.

numbers.k: US troops in Vietnam at end of term

numbers.v: ~36,800 (1964–1968), the majority of the war's total

decisions: NSAM 273, four days after Dallas: the objective is to help Saigon win; the withdrawal plan is quietly dropped.
Tonkin Gulf resolution passes 416–0 and 88–2 after an attack on 2 August and a second on 4 August that the NSA's own history says did not happen.
Rolling Thunder approved; sustained bombing of the North begins 2 March.
3,500 Marines land at Da Nang to guard the air base: the first combat units.
'We will stand in Vietnam': 50,000 more troops announced at a midday press conference, 125,000 in all, with more to follow; no reserve call-up, no declaration, no tax.
Westmoreland's requests approved in steps to 525,000; the war of attrition and the body count.
The Wise Men, reconvened, tell him to disengage. Clifford, new at Defense, agrees.
Announces a bombing halt north of the 20th parallel, talks, and that he will not seek re-election.
Full bombing halt; Paris talks expand. Nixon's campaign, through Anna Chennault, urges Saigon to stall.

advisers.note: Never wavered.
Escalated it, doubted it by 1966, commissioned the Pentagon Papers in 1967, and left for the World Bank in February 1968.
Came in a hawk, examined the numbers for a month, and turned the president.
The 'fork in the road' memo (Jan 1965) and the Pleiku visit that started sustained bombing.
The last optimist; filtered the intelligence the president saw.
The in-house dissenter; his 1965 memos argued for a compromise exit and were heard and rejected.
Pressed for reserves and wider bombing; after Tet asked for 206,000 more men, which leaked and broke the consensus.
Search and destroy; 'the light at the end of the tunnel' (Nov 1967); Tet two months later.
Took over in June 1968; shifted to clear-and-hold and pacification.
Opposed sending ground troops as ambassador, having been the general who militarised the mission.
Second tour.
Carried over to Nixon; Thieu's steady supporter.
The agency's order-of-battle estimates were higher than MACV's and were suppressed in the 1967 compromise.
Ran pacification and the Phoenix program.
'Blowtorch Bob'; pacification with a management chart.

advisers.post: Deputy Secretary of Defense; Paris negotiator

advisers.note: Left, in part, over the war.
Advised while sitting on the Court.
Opposed the February 1965 bombing in a memo and was frozen out for a year.

advisers.who: Dean Acheson and the Wise Men
advisers.note: Endorsed the war in November 1967; reversed in March 1968. Acheson, Ball, Bundy, Dillon, Vance, Bradley, Ridgway, Taylor, Lodge, Murphy, Goldberg, Fortas, Dean.
Ran the air war and wanted it unrestricted.

text: Johnson: from 16,000 to 536,000, the resolution, the bombing, Tet, the Wise Men, and the night he quit.
